title: Price-band routing and fallback-variant gating with tenant budget caps
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Goal: implement a price-band aware routing layer that gates region and GPU selection against per-tenant budget caps and automatically escalates/downgrades to validated fallback model variants when spot/on-demand economics or eviction risk exceed configured thresholds. Rationale: current fallback behavior is coarse (region-first then model variant) and often causes expensive on-demand fallthroughs for tenants with tight budgets. This ticket designs a fast scoring function (price band + eviction risk + latency delta) and an admission controller which applies soft budget caps and graceful variant degradation (e.g., switch to 8-bit quantized variant or smaller context model) rather than immediate request rejection. Key constraints: keep decision latency under 3ms on the routing path, preserve existing SLOs for P0 tenants, and integrate with existing tenant spend metering and console guards.
acceptance_criteria: Routing evaluates price-band and eviction-risk per region within the runtime <= 3ms median
Per-tenant soft budget cap configurable and enforced with adjustable grace headroom
Fallback variant transitions are orchestrated without request loss and documented in rollout logs
End-to-end e2e test that simulates spot eviction surge and verifies graceful model variant degradation and cost delta reporting
Dashboard shows per-tenant spend forecast when price-bands trigger fallback within 10 minutes of decision
design_decisions: Use a four-tier price-band index (cheap, normal, elevated, premium) computed from spot/on-demand ratio and current market price feeds
Score GPU families with a composite metric: price_band_score * eviction_risk_factor + latency_penalty, normalized per-region
Implement soft caps: when tenant spend >= cap * 0.9, start preferring degraded variants and smaller GPUs; when >= cap, throttle to configured rate limit rather than block
Fallback variants: prefer quantized variant of same model -> narrower context variant -> instruction-tuned smaller model -> deny/route to paid overflow
Decision state persisted as short-lived tokens (TTL 30s) to avoid recomputation for bursty request patterns
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting. Aligned on price-band telemetry inputs (cloud market API + internal preemption metrics). Assigned Ethan to implement scoring service and Marina to own policy config schema.

2026-02-25: Prototype scoring lib checked in (internal repo: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proto PR#412). Benchmarks show 1.8ms median add-on on routing path when run as local in-process library.

2026-03-01: Integration spike with tenant meter completed. Found race where two parallel requests could both pick on-demand fallback and overshoot soft cap; adding atomic spend reservation to routing admission controller.

2026-03-04: Design review feedback from PM and Console teams: add explicit audit log entries for variant transitions and surface events to Console rollout timeline. Added console-event contract to design.
2026-03-05: Added e2e test harness that simulates price-band shift and spot eviction. Next: implement throttling step and finalize rollout plan for runtime-1.28 canary pool.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misclassification of price-band could cause SLO regression for latency-sensitive tenants. Mitigation: start with conservative premium threshold and rollout to non-P0 tenants only
Risk: spend reservation race could allow brief overspend. Mitigation: implement atomic decrementing reservation and enforced cooldown window per-tenant
Risk: increased routing latency. Mitigation: keep scoring lib in-process and fall back to cached tokens with 30s TTL to amortize cost
implementation_notes: Add new config schema in routing policy: price_band_thresholds, soft_cap_headroom_pct, fallback_variant_sequence, throttle_policy
Expose metrics: routing.price_band.choice, routing.variant.transition, routing.spend.reservation_outcome, routing.latency.addon_ms
Console: consume variant transition audit events and display tenant-level cost implications in rollout panel
Testing: unit tests for scoring, integration test with simulated market feed, chaos test for spot eviction spike
next_steps: Finalize throttling semantics (fixed window vs token-bucket) by 2026-03-08
Complete atomic spend reservation implementation and bench by 2026-03-12
Schedule runtime-1.28 canary (10% of non-P0 traffic) 2026-03-18 after Console changes deployed
